content:
Adobe Commerce and AEM are moving closer together, from the airport website to the product page.

In this issue

  • Who's "Really" on Adobe Commerce? Take a look at Alshaya, they run stores for brands like H&M and Starbucks in the Middle East.
  • Where The Pieces Meet. Adobe's Commerce architecture guide splits the work into a commerce backend, a storefront and connected services.
  • Not Just a Payment Company. Some SaaS products advertise themselves as an ecommerce company, but when you look at the numbers, the majority of their revenue comes from payments.
  • You Pair Food Why Not Your Platform? Adobe documents more than one way to use their suite of products: Commerce Storefront on Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service, Commerce Optimizer for merchants on other commerce systems, and headless AEM.
  • Where Magento Fits. Adobe bought Magento and renamed it Adobe Commerce.
  • Data and research. Heathrow's announced work. The October 8 release names AEM and Brand Visibility for Heathrow's website and AI search accuracy.
